headline: WFP Says War and Shipping Costs Could Endanger Aid
deck: Thirty percent of global fertilizer supplies flow through the Strait of Hormuz, where WFP expects delayed agricultural effects.
body: World Food Programme said it could incur $727 million in additional costs by mid-2027 if current dynamics persist, putting assistance for 7.3 million people around the world at risk. [E1]

Thirty percent of global fertilizer supplies flow directly through the Strait of Hormuz, the agency said, which it expects to have a delayed effect on agricultural output as smallholder farms contend with El Niño. [E2]

Attacks in the Black Sea continue to disrupt food exports, with implications for food security beyond the region. [E3] From June through October, OHCHR recorded reports of 164 attacks on commercial vessels in Ukraine’s Odesa and Mykolaiv regions and in the Black Sea; it has verified 15 attacks in which at least 21 vessel workers were killed and 43 injured. [E4][E5]
The paper’s 17 November report recorded a tanker disabled in the Strait of Hormuz; WFP’s current statement projects additional costs and aid at risk if present dynamics persist. [E1][E6]
